lightPrompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: one distinct OPDA editorial pastel-watercolour header for an ontology-modelling chapter.
Composition: ultra-wide shallow panoramic 3:1 landscape. Arrange a single concrete scene side-to-side, complete subjects with visible margins, composed for a 1024px-wide website. Not a montage, grid, chart, diagram or screenshot.
Style: refined professional architectural sketchbook illustration; expressive organic deep-purple pen-and-ink contours, soft translucent pastel watercolour and softly opaque gouache, visible pigment variation, paper highlights, clear recognisable silhouettes and tactile material detail. Warm, colourful and humane, not childish.
Light palette: cool off-white #F9F9F9 paper reaching every edge, deep-purple #231F2F ink, generous OPDA gold #FEC92B, petrol teal #0E8478, violet #6C5BD4, rose and coral. Colour substantial object surfaces. No beige or sepia cast.
Constraints: absolutely no letters, words, numbers, labels, symbols, logos, watermark, signature, readable handwriting or personal information. No photography, 3D rendering, glossy plastic, glow, neon, floating icons, jigsaw pieces, arrows, checkmarks or approval stamps. This is an editorial metaphor, not evidence or formal notation. No computer dashboards or implied running application.
darkPrompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: dark-mode counterpart of an OPDA editorial watercolour header.
Input image: the supplied approved light illustration is the EDIT TARGET.
Change only paper, ink values and pigment palette. Preserve the exact objects and people, identity, object count, arrangement, relative sizes, proportions, poses, perspective, framing, crop, negative space and image aspect ratio.
Dark palette: flat deep-purple paper #131224 reaching every edge; rich pastel gold, petrol teal, violet, rose and coral watercolour and softly opaque gouache. Use pale lavender and off-white fine ink only where needed for legibility. Paper is deep purple, never black, grey or brown. Keep a calm, colourful, professional magazine illustration.
No redesign, additions, removals, relayout, night scenery, stars, inversion filter, glow, fluorescent outlines, neon, letters, text, digits, labels, signatures or watermarks. This is a palette edit, not a new scene.

export.operation: Whole-image proportional resize; no crop or forced frame. Actual quality and source/export dimensions are recorded per asset.

pages.title: Ontology modelling
pages.prompt: A wide architectural teaching atelier seen from a low oblique angle: a long transparent geometric pavilion skeleton is being carefully assembled from petrol timber struts by two model-makers standing at opposite ends; small gold model walls, violet joint samples and a rolled blank drawing rest beside it. Emphasise deliberately chosen connections and human judgement, not constructing a real building. No rows of cards or seated workshop.
pages.alt: Two model-makers examining the structure and connections of a pavilion maquette.

pages.title: Foundations and modelling judgement
pages.prompt: A precise yet lyrical horizontal conservation still life centred on one teal handheld torch, with its removable gold battery, coral end cap, violet lens ring and plain balance pan arranged beside it. Keep the main torch assembly recognisable while selected removable parts expose how its identity and functional whole are considered. A thin articulated magnifying lens studies the assembly. No written measurement marks or numerals, no duplicate torches.
pages.alt: A torch and its removable components invite questions about identity, dependence and the unity of a whole.

pages.title: Choose the right representation
pages.prompt: A shallow museum-style display of tangible representation studies: one lilac plaster architectural building maquette at the left, its separate petrol wireframe outline drawing held upright behind a gold frame at centre, and two differently shaped ceramic relationship joints lying independently at right. The physical object, its separate representation and connectors have different silhouettes and materials. No house cutaway, figures, letters, graphs or technical symbols.
pages.alt: A building maquette, a separate framed representation and distinct connector samples show different representational choices.

pages.title: Identity through roles and change
pages.prompt: One single carved wooden human figure remains centred on a wide felt mat; two removable textile sashes in teal and coral lie separately on either side, each beside its own folded unlettered transaction document. Behind the same figure sits a short violet garment rack, not another person. The stable bearer and detachable contextual roles remain visibly distinct. Calm sculptural still life, no faces, no second figure, no badges or icons.
pages.alt: One figure remains distinct from two removable role sashes and their separate transaction papers.

pages.title: Connect meanings across contexts
pages.prompt: An architectural seam study with two distinct independently supported structures: a violet brick colonnade on the left and a petrol timber framed arcade on the right. A carefully detailed gold articulated joint lies at their meeting boundary, with each structure retaining its own material and character. A narrow coral tracing overlay reveals the junction, not a connecting bridge across water. Show established structures and the precise agreement at their seam. No people, arrows or labels.
pages.alt: Two established structures retain their distinct character while a carefully examined joint connects them.

pages.title: Evidence, claims and time
pages.prompt: An elongated archival still life: one small wall specimen with a hairline crack stands at left beside a surveyor's folded unlettered field sketch; two translucent sheets showing revised drawings of that same crack step across the middle; at right a shallow open violet archival folder receives the later sheet. A delicate unmarked brass hourglass sits behind, not a calendar or clock face. Distinguish one observed subject from evolving records without duplicated buildings.
pages.alt: One wall specimen sits beside an original field sketch, revised account sheets and an archival folder.

pages.title: From a useful question to a reviewable candidate
pages.prompt: A close side-on view of two hands opening a wide petrol folio to reveal a carefully constructed small room maquette and loose contextual study drawings; a gold pencil points to one specific threshold detail rather than the whole model. One coral alternative wall piece remains aside for comparison. The folio is a proposal being inspected, not an approved plan. No text or building skyline.
pages.alt: An opened candidate folio combines a room model, supporting sketches and an alternative detail for review.

pages.title: Scope and package: eight concerns, six connected outputs
pages.prompt: A shallow flat-lay of one unbound architectural portfolio with several different material leaves fanning from a shared spine: translucent tracing paper, heavy violet board, a petrol linen swatch, a gold folded contour sheet, coral tissue and a small wire detail plate. All are related samples gathered for one review; retain distinct forms rather than six drawers or a grid. A simple cotton tie loosely gathers the portfolio, not a postal package.
pages.alt: Different review materials fan from one portfolio spine while retaining their separate forms.

pages.title: Vocabularies and classification: choose what the list means
pages.prompt: A botanical-classification-inspired architecture still life: three differently shaped pressed leaves in violet, petrol and gold are arranged along an open herbarium sheet, with a branching living sprig at one end and a shallow round tray of distinct seed specimens at the other. Blank coral paper tabs stay attached to individual specimens but carry no marks. Contrast organised choices, a growing population and descriptive facets without presenting a formal taxonomy or card rail.
pages.alt: Pressed specimens, a living branch and separate seed samples suggest different kinds of organised lists.

pages.title: Mapping records: correspondence with an inspectable argument
pages.prompt: A conservator's comparison scene seen from overhead: two distinct ornate architectural ceramic fragments, one petrol and one violet, are set side by side on separate cotton pads. A gold flexible profile gauge traces one edge while a narrow translucent coral sheet records the contour between them. The fragments remain separate and visibly differ; matching a contour does not make them identical. No jigsaw fit, merging, chain links or arrows.
pages.alt: Two distinct architectural fragments are compared through a contour record without being merged.

pages.title: Meaning, checks and delivery: four jobs, four contracts
pages.prompt: An instrument maker's shallow horizontal bench with a single violet frame prototype at left, a separate teal transparent tolerance stencil resting over a sheet at centre, and a gold caliper inspecting one opening at right. One intentionally shorter coral sample strip lies below to invite a counterexample. Real tactile tools show a designed thing and a distinct checking template, with no readable scales, pass marks or machine dashboard.
pages.alt: A frame prototype, separate checking stencil and contrasting sample show that design and checking are different activities.

pages.title: Sensitivity and policy: model privacy, roles and scope
pages.prompt: A quiet archive consultation still life: a translucent petrol privacy screen partly shades an unlettered folded report on one side, while an open violet reference book on the other shows only an abstract line drawing of the report's structure. A coral ribbon marks a limited span on the loose report, not the entire shelf. Gold paper weights hold the materials. Distinguish describing information from exposing its contents, no padlocks, shields, eyes, keys, people or security interface.
pages.alt: An open reference book describes a document while a separate report remains partly screened and scoped.

pages.title: Languages and profiles: choose the tool for the question
pages.prompt: A colourful compact architect's tool roll lies horizontally unrolled: a deep violet drafting pen, petrol fine brush, gold divider compasses, coral flat stencil and lavender magnifying lens each have their own stitched pocket. Nearby one modest unlettered construction study is marked only with drawn geometry. Tools remain different and selected for different tasks; no logos, text, digits, rulers with numbers or literal software symbols.
pages.alt: A tool roll holds distinct drawing, measuring and examining tools for different modelling questions.

pages.title: The decisions behind the method
pages.prompt: A side-view still life of a review archive: three upright richly pigmented bound reference volumes sit at left, a large open decision ledger at centre has blank pages and a coral folded amendment slip resting visibly over an earlier translucent sheet, and a gold page weight holds a narrow chosen passage. No readable writing, official seals, approval stamps or courthouse imagery. Emphasise scope, layered amendments and inspectable authority rather than judgement by software.
pages.alt: Reference volumes and an open ledger preserve a decision alongside a visibly separate amendment.

pages.title: Namespaces and identifiers
pages.prompt: A horizontal miniature reference library with two visibly separate shelving bays: one houses a few abstract geometric vocabulary masters in violet and teal, the other holds several small individual specimen models each tied with a different entirely blank durable gold tag. A thin coral catalogue ribbon points to one shelf compartment without connecting all objects. Different shelf homes and stable blank tags illustrate namespace governance and identity, not a database. No drawers, addresses, text, digits or hierarchy arrows.
pages.alt: Separate library bays hold vocabulary masters and individually tagged specimens, suggesting distinct naming families.

pages.title: From source evidence to model decisions
pages.prompt: A long editorial landscape seen across a low reading desk: an old folded architectural source drawing in violet rests at far left under a clear glass weight; a real small petrol roof-junction specimen occupies the middle; a fresh coral-and-gold clay study at right deliberately differs from the original drawing. A single hand holds a thin tracing overlay away from the new model, comparing evidence without copying its structure. No diagram arrows, text, dates, numbers or pipeline machinery.
pages.alt: A source drawing and physical specimen inform a different candidate model rather than being copied into it.
